subject: Automotive & EVs
title: The DeLorean DMC-12
description: A quick win: understand The DeLorean DMC-12.

hook.text: The DeLorean is famous for time travel—in a movie. In real life, it was a beautiful disaster.

buildup.text: John DeLorean left GM to build a stainless steel sports car with gull-wing doors in Northern Ireland.

discovery.text: The brushed steel body looked stunning. But the underpowered V6 made it slower than most sedans.

twist.text: Only about 9,000 were built before the company collapsed. DeLorean was arrested in a scandal.

climax.text: Then 'Back to the Future' made it the most recognizable car in cinema history.

punchline.text: A failed car became an immortal movie star.

quiz.question: What was the DeLorean's real-life biggest problem?
options: It was too expensive to produce

details.summary: The DeLorean DMC-12, famous as the Back to the Future time machine, was a gull-winged stainless steel sports car that became a cultural icon despite commercial failure and its creator's downfall.
details.whyItMatters: The DeLorean shows how a single movie appearance can immortalize a car. Its story also serves as a cautionary tale about automotive entrepreneurship and overpromising on technology.
takeaways: Its brushed stainless steel body required no paint
Only about 9,000 were built before the company collapsed in 1983
The Back to the Future franchise made it one of the most recognizable cars

faq.question: Was the DeLorean actually a good car?
faq.answer: Reviews were mixed. The underpowered V6 engine and poor build quality disappointed buyers. Its styling and gull-wing doors were innovative, but the driving experience did not match the futuristic looks.

faq.question: Is DeLorean making a comeback?
faq.answer: A new DeLorean Motor Company has announced plans for an electric sports car inspired by the original. Several attempts have been made to revive the brand, though none has reached mass production yet.
